sácanlos: sacar + los — they drive them out, take them out (present 3rd pl. + object los; = los sacan)
de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each' · also de — 'in respect of' after an adjective (sobejana de mala 'exceedingly bad'); 'with regard to, about' (me plaze de mio Çid 'I am pleased about the Cid'); 'from, at the hand of' (de señor non ha graçia 'he gets no favor from a lord'); 'from' of origin (de moros fo 'it came from Moors'); 'at' of manner (de vagar 'at leisure', de + the noun vagar) · also de’ — Pidal's de’llaño, read as del llaño 'of the plain' (the article's l run into the ll; a reading, not certain) · de + infinitive after an adjective (de ir somos guisados 'we are ready to go') · also de + infinitive after a verb: començar de 'to begin to' (compeçó de fablar 'he began to speak'), piénssanse de 'set about' (piénssanse de armar), aver de 'to have to' (lo que ha de far 'what he has to do') · also de — 'within' of a time limit (De aquestos quinze días, most likely 'within these fifteen days'; sense uncertain); de veluntad 'willingly'; de + superlative partitive (de los mejores guarnimientos 'of the best equipment') · also de — 'with, from' of the means or source (diziendo de la boca 'saying with his mouth'; de cuer les pesa 'it grieves them from the heart') · also de que 'of whom, of which' (relative after a noun; de moros de que non avien sabor 'of Moors they had no taste for')
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
en: en — in, into, on · en — of it, thence (= ende; por en avemos qué fablar 'of which we have to speak') · also en — 'as' (en paria 'as tribute'); en essora 'at that moment' · also en — 'among' (en todos los sos 'among all his men') · also en + infinitive 'in (doing)' (en levarlo adelant 'in carrying it forward'); en çinco días 'in five days'
alcaz: alcaz — pursuit, chase (verbal noun of alcançar; en alcaz 'in pursuit'; modern alcance means 'reach', closest persecución)
tanto: tanto — so much, so great · tanto quanto + subjunctive 'as long as' (tanto quanto yo biva 'as long as I live') · also tanto — 'so many' before a masc. sg. noun used collectively (tanto palafré, tanto buen pendón 'so many a palfrey, so many a good banner'; = tantos) · also dos tanto — 'twice as much' (que vos meresca dos tanto 'that I may deserve it of you twice over'; = el doble)
braço: braço — arm (= brazo); braço' = braços, the plural with its s lost before las
con: con — with · also con — 'with the help of' (con Dios 'with God's help'; verlo hemos con Dios 'we shall see it with God's help')
loriga: loriga — coat of mail, hauberk (= loriga, now only a historical term; cota de malla is the usual word)
veriedes: veer — you would have seen (conditional 2nd pl.; = veríais; the minstrel's aside to the audience)
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day') · also a — 'has' before the participle, agreeing with the object (la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; a menester 'has need of'); a + dative of the person affected (a Minaya matáronle el cavallo 'they killed Minaya's horse') · a — 'as, for' (tóvoslo a grand fonta 'he took it as a great affront') · also a — 'with' of instrument (a dientes las tomó 'with his teeth he took them'; = con) · also prender a espolonada — 'to begin the attack, charge' (priso a espolonada, Pidal 'comenzó el ataque'); pendón a corças 'a banner with (a device of) roe-does' (a = 'with', likely)
part: part — share, portion (noun; = parte) · also part — side (del otra part 'on the other side'; = parte) · also a part — aside, apart (a part salidos son 'they have gone aside') · also aver part con uno — 'to stand in someone's favour' (con él avedes part 'you have favour with him', Pidal 'tenéis con él favor, acogida')
tantas: tanto — so many (fem. pl.; tantas lanças 'so many lances'; = tantas)
que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque) · por que — by which, whereby (por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more') · also que — 'so that, lest' introducing purpose/result (que por miedo non dexen nada; por tal lo faze … que no lo ventasse nadi); after después/mientra 'after, while' (después que, mientra que) · also que — than, after a comparative (mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him') · also que — what (indirect interrogative; dezir vos he que faze 'I shall tell you what he does'; = qué)
por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain') · also por — 'in' after fiar (yo fío por Dios 'I trust in God') · also por — 'to fetch, for' after enbiar/ir (enbiaré por ellas, irán por ellas 'I shall send for them', 'they will go for them'); por cuenta 'by count, in a count' · also por — as (por heredad 'as a possession') · also por — 'about, after' with preguntar (por el rey tómanse a preguntar 'they begin to ask after the king'); por + infinitive 'for … to' (por … vençer reyes, 'for … to defeat kings')
el: el — the (masc.) · also el — 'he who' before a relative (el qui quisiere, el que es sobre Fenares); el before a fem. noun beginning with a vowel (el espada = la espada; el algara = la algara) · also el de + place name 'he of, the one from' (mio Çid el de Bivar)
campo: campo — field, open ground, field of battle (= campo; en el campo 'in the open field'; the element in Campeador) · campo de Taranz 'the plain of Taranz'
caden: caer — they fall (to), are due (present 3rd pl. with -d- kept; caden çient marcos 'a hundred marks fall to each'; = caen, closest les corresponden)
sin: sin — without · also sin — 'besides, apart from' (sin las peonadas 'besides the foot-soldiers'); sin falla 'without fail'; sin dubda
dueños: dueño — master, owner, lord (pl.; a dueños e a cavallos 'for masters and horses'; = dueños)
salir: salir — to come out, emerge (infinitive; salir vermejos en sangre 'to come out red with blood'; = salir)
partes: parte — part, quarter, direction (pl.); de todas partes 'from every quarter'
complidos: complido — full, complete, finished (past part. of complir, masc. pl.; nueve meses complidos 'nine months full'; = cumplidos)
duró: durar — it lasted (preterite 3rd sg.; = duró) · also durar — he spent, took (time) (en ganar aquellas villas mio Çid duró tres años; Pidal 'tardó, empleó, gastó')
segudar: segudar — to pursue (infinitive; Pidal 'perseguir'; used as a noun, el segudar 'the pursuit'; no modern segudar, = perseguir, as a noun persecución)
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least' · also a + el standing for a + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (al espada = a la espada) · also al — 'other thing, the rest' (neuter, Latin alius; de lo al non pienssan nada 'of anything else they think nothing'; distinct from a + el) · also a + el before an infinitive 'on, upon' (al exir de Salón 'on leaving the Jalón'; = al salir) · al 'the other thing, the rest' in al feredes adelant 'the rest you will do later' · also por al 'otherwise, for any other reason' (non passará por al 'it will not be otherwise'); a mí mandedes al 'order me something else', give me another charge (the likelier reading of a terse line)
búcar: Búcar — Búcar, the Moorish king who comes against Valencia (personal name, Arabic; no modern Spanish form beyond Búcar)
acá: acá — here, hither (adverb; exidos somos acá 'we have come out to here'; = acá)
mar: mar — sea (here fem., la mar salada; = mar, now usually masc.)
la: el/la — the (fem.); her/it (object pronoun) · also la que 'the one that' (Çelfa la que dizen de Canal 'Çelfa, the one they call of the Canal')
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us') · also reflexive 'ourselves' (nos partimos 'we part'); dative (la missa nos dirá 'will say for us') · also nos' — non + se (aun nos' van del campo 'they are still not leaving the field'; the apostrophe marks the elision) · also nos — non + se, written without apostrophe (nin amigo a amigo nos pueden consolar 'nor can friend console friend'; mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him', the no redundant after the comparison)
hemos: aver — we will/shall (1st pl. future auxiliary; restored by Pidal in the split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos)
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold') · also aver — 'I will', the future auxiliary in a split future (quitarvos e … darvos e de mano 'I will free you … I will let you go'; = vos quitaré, vos daré) · also the full verb 'I have' (el sabor que dend e 'the delight I have of it')
respuso: responder — he answered (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = respondió)
dios: Dios — God · also Dios! — interjection of wonder (Dios, cómmo se alabavan! 'God, how they boasted!')
tal: tal — such; por tal 'for such a reason, for this purpose' (= tal) · also tal … commo — 'such … as' (tal juego commo iva por la cort 'such sport as went round the court')
amiztad: amiztad — friendship (fem. noun; = amistad; Pidal's [a]mi[z]tad, editorial letters; the el before it is the article el for la)
tienes: tener + se — he holds himself (present 3rd sg. tiene + reflexive se, the e of se run into tiene; tener por 'to consider as'; = se tiene)
mano: mano — hand (sg.); en vuestra mano = 'in your keeping' · a mano 'by hand, hand-picked' (escollechos a mano 'chosen by hand') · dar de mano 'to let go, release' (Pidal 'soltar'; darvos e de mano 'I will let you go')
aguijar: aguijar — to spur (one's horse), ride hard
así: así — thus, so; así como 'as soon as'
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como) · how, that, in the way that (commo sirva a doña Ximena 'how he is to serve doña Ximena'); like (commo la uña de la carne) · also commo si + imperfect subjunctive — 'as if' (commo si escapasse 'as if he were fleeing') · commo que 'as one who' (commo que ira a de rey … es echado 'as one who has the king's anger and is cast out') · also commo — 'as soon as, when' (commo gelo a dicho 'as soon as he told it him'); 'since, as' (commo fío por Dios 'as I trust in God')
semeja: semejar — it seems, appears (present 3rd sg.; = parece)
mi: mi — my (unstressed possessive) · also mi — me (stressed pronoun after a preposition; por mi 'on my behalf'; = mí)
ensayar: ensayar — to try, use (a weapon) (infinitive; querríalas ensayar 'I should like to try them (the arms) out', Pidal 'probar, usar un arma'); also 'to attack' (idlos ensayar 'go and attack them', Pidal 'acometer'; = probar; acometer)
mas: mas — but · also mas — 'most' (superlative, = más; en todo lo mas alto 'on the very highest part') · also mas — 'more' comparative (que es mas ondrada 'which is more honored'; = más)
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!' · si non — otherwise, if not (si non, do sopiéredes 'if not, wherever you learn'); si + future subjunctive 'if' (si nos falláredes 'if you find us') · also si — si'nulla = sin + nulla with -n assimilated before n- (si'nulla dubda 'without any fear' (or 'doubt'); = sin ningún miedo, sin ninguna duda) · also si non — 'except, but for' (si non a estos cavalleros 'except these knights'; = salvo) · also si — 'so', optative, = sí, with the present subjunctive in an adjuration (si vos vala el Criador 'so may the Creator help you')
o: o — or; also ó — where (interrogative, Latin ubi; ¿O sodes…? 'Where are you…?') · also o — where (relative adverb; o dizen Castejón 'which they call Castejón'; o el Campeador estava 'where the Campeador was'; = donde) · correlative 'either … or' (o me dexaredes … o … levaredes 'either you will leave me … or you will take away')
comigo: comigo — with me (con + migo, Latin mecum; = conmigo)
cade: caer — falls (present 3rd sg., cade with its -d- kept; Pidal's restoration [cade]; cade en alcança 'falls in pursuit', i.e. gives chase, an idiom whose sense is taken from context; = cae)
te: te — you, thee (2nd sg. object pronoun)
fata: fata — until, as far as (variant of fasta; = hasta)
aquí: aquí — here; d'aquí 'from here' · also 'then, at this point' (aquí dixo el comde 'then the count said')
verdad: verdad — truth (dezir vos he la verdad 'I shall tell you the truth'; = verdad) · also non será verdad — 'it shall not be so' (Pidal: 'esto no será así'; esto non será verdad)
tiene: tener — he has (present 3rd sg.) · also tener en cuenta — 'he takes account of, counts' (non tiene en cuenta 'he does not keep count'; = tiene en cuenta)
bavieca: Bavieca — Babieca, the Cid's horse (proper name; = Babieca)
va: ir — he/she goes (present 3rd sg.; = va); ir + gerund, 'to be (gradually) doing' · ir + infinitive 'goes to' (la manol va besar 'goes to kiss his hand', el Duero va passar 'goes to cross the Duero') · also va — 'there is, goes on' impersonal (¡Qué priessa va en los moros! 'what a stir there is among the Moors!')
del: de + el — of the (contraction) · also del standing for de + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (del albergada = de la albergada) · also del — 'from, for, because of' (cause; del gozo 'from the joy'; del çerviçio 'for the service')
arriba: arriba — up, upward (adverb; = arriba) · also postposed 'up, upstream' (Fenares arriba 'up the Henares'; desí arriba 'from there upward')
colada: Colada — Colada, a sword, won by the Çid at Tévar (hi gañó a Colada 'there he won Colada'; = Colada)
un: uno — a, one (apocopated masc. before a noun)
colpe: colpe — blow, stroke, instance (= golpe); a tod el primer colpe 'at the very first go'
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha) · ha — to (a with h-, aver a + inf. 'will, must': lo an todos ha far 'all are to do it'); aver — has, possesses (las fijas que ha 'the daughters she has') · also ha — future ending after infinitive + clitics, the split future (tornar nos la ha 'he will give it back to us'; = nos la tornará) · also ha — there is, there are (impersonal; dos señas ha cabdales 'there are two chief banners'; = hay) · also ha — perfect auxiliary 'has' before the participle (ha vendido 'has sold'; fechos los ha ricos 'has made them rich') · also 'has, gets' (de señor non ha graçia 'he has no favor from a lord') · also ha de + inf. 'is to' (que los ha de aguardar 'who is to attend them'; aver de + infinitive, = ha de) · also non ha qui + inf. — 'there is no one to' (impersonal ha 'there is'; non ha qui tomallos 'there is no one to take them'; = no hay quien) · also ha — of time elapsed, 'it is, it has been' (Pocos días ha … que 'it is a few days since'; = hace)
carbonclas: carbonclas — carbuncles, red gems set in the helmet as ornament (fem. pl., from Latin carbunculus; Pidal 'carbunclos' o rubíes; = carbunclos, carbúnculos)
gelas: ge + las — them for/to him (ge, ancestor of modern se, + las; = se las) · also ge 'to them' (non gelas do yo 'I do not give them to them')
cortól: cortar + le — cortó 'he cut' (preterite 3rd sg.) + l(e) 'him' (enclitic; = le cortó)
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision') · also todo — adverbial 'wholly, all over' before an adjective (todo suzio 'all filthy')
lo: lo — him, it (object pronoun) · lo que perdedes 'that which you lose' (neuter antecedent of the relative) · also lo — neuter article 'what is' (lo to 'what is yours'); pleonastic 'it' (lo an, lo han a far; por tal lo faze 'for that reason he does it')
llegado: llegar — arrived (past part.; era llegado 'had arrived', ser as perfect auxiliary; = llegado)
allén: allén — beyond (preposition with de; allén de Teruel 'beyond Teruel'; = allende)
ganó: ganar — he won, conquered (preterite 3rd sg.; la que en buen punto ganó 'which he won in a good hour'; = ganó)
marcos: marco — mark (a unit of weight for silver, pl.)
d: de — of, with (elided form of de before a vowel, d'arena = de arena) · de — from (unos d'otros 'one from another') · also d — 'about, concerning' (D' iffantes de Carrión yo vos quiero contar 'of the Infantes of Carrión I wish to tell you'; = de)
val: valer — help! (imperative 2nd sg., apocopated for vale; = vale) · val — valley (noun, = valle; el val de río Martín 'the valley of the river Martín') · also valer — he helps, avails (present 3rd sg., apocopated for vale; si no nos val 'if he does not help us'; = vale)
batalla: batalla — battle (= batalla; exir a batalla 'to sally out to battle')
aquís: aquí + se — then + reflexive (aquí 'at this point, then' + se; aquís metió en nuevas, Pidal 'entonces hizo cosa señalada', 'then he did a notable thing'; = aquí se)
ondró: ondrar — he honoured, made honoured (preterite 3rd sg.; por o ondró su barba 'through which he honoured his beard'; = honró)
quantos: quanto — as many as (masc. pl.; todos quantos 'all who'; = cuantos)
elle: elle — he (old form of él, Latin ille; elle fizo = él hizo; Pidal restores el[le])
están: estar — they are, stay (present 3rd pl.; = están) · also progressive auxiliary with a gerund (bendiziéndol están 'they are blessing him')
yas: ya + se — already … themselves (ya + reflexive se cut to s; yas mueven 'they are already moving'; = ya se)
ivan: ir — they were going (imperfect 3rd pl.; ivan posar 'they were going to lodge'; = iban) · also ir + gerund, 'were coming to, gradually' (ya lo ivan provando 'they were by now coming to experience it')
tornando: tornar — turning (gerund; la cabeça tornando va 'he goes turning his head'; = tornando)
sabet: saber — know, mark you (imperative 2nd pl., sabed; sabet = sabed; epic tag addressed to the audience)
firme: firme — firm; used adverbially, 'firmly, securely' (= firmemente) · also firme' — firmes, 'firm, steadfast' (adjective plural, final s dropped; firme' son los moros 'the Moors are firm', i.e. still holding their ground)
robavan: robar — they were plundering (imperfect 3rd pl.; robavan el campo 'they stripped the field'; = robaban)
llegados: llegar — arrived, come (past part. masc. pl. after the auxiliary seer; quando son llegados 'when they have come'; = llegados)
buena: bueno — good (fem.); en buen(a) '(born/girded) in a good hour' — the poem's honorific formula
nasco: nacer — he was born (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = nació)
roy: Roy — Ruy, short for Rodrigo (Roy Díaz = Rodrigo Díaz, the Cid)
diaz: Díaz — Díaz (patronymic 'son of Diego'; Ruy Diaz, the Cid's name, = Ruy Díaz; same as díaz, here without accent)
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
contado: contar — renowned, esteemed (past part. used as a standing epithet of the Campeador) · also of others: un Burgalés contado, 'a renowned man of Burgos' (Martín Antolínez)
dos: dos — two · also do + se, 'when/where … (they)' (Dos fallan con los moros 'when they come upon the Moors', Pidal 'cuando se encuentran'; = cuando se encuentran) · also do + se, 'where … (he might)' with a subjunctive (non vido … dos alçasse 'he saw nowhere he might hide', Pidal 'donde se escondiese')
él: él — he (stressed subject pronoun) · also él — 'him, it' after a preposition, of a thing (a él vino; en él fincaredes 'in it', i.e. in Castejón)
algo: algo — something; the poem's discreet word for money, wealth
cara: cara — face · also de cara 'face to face, facing the enemy' (lidiando de cara 'fighting face to face')
fronzida: fronzir — gathered, drawn up in folds (past part. fem., agreeing with cofia; la cofia fronzida, Pidal 'fruncida sobre la cara', the coif drawn up about the face; = fruncida) · also fronzida trahe la cara 'he has his face gathered', Pidal: understood of the coif gathered about the face (fruncida)
almófar: almófar — hood of mail worn over the head and neck (word of Arabic origin; almófar a cuestas 'the mail hood thrown back on the shoulders'; = almófar)
cofia: cofia — coif, the close cap worn under the helmet or hood of mail (cofia fronzida 'the coif wrinkled/gathered'; = cofia)
sobre: sobre — upon, over; here 'on the security of' (sobre aquellas arcas) · sobre Navas de Palos 'above, hard by Navas de Palos' (position along the route) · also 'before, against (a town to be besieged)' (sobre Alcoçer iva posar 'went to camp before Alcocer') · also sobre — 'besides, in addition to' (Sobre aquesto todo 'on top of all this') · also sobre — around (Pidal 'alrededor de', comp. v. 1053; fincan sobre so señor 'they stand around their lord')
los: el — the (masc. pl.); them (object pronoun) · also los que 'those who' (demonstrative use before a relative); los — him, them as object of consejar (commo los consejava 'as he advised them') · also los de 'those of' (con los de Castejón 'with the men of Castejón')
della: de + ella — 'from/of her/it' (contraction); della e della part, 'from the one and the other side', i.e. from all sides (= de ella, here de una y otra parte)
sos: so — his, her, their (= modern sus) · also los sos 'his own men' (possessive with article as noun; en todos los sos 'among all his men')
van: ir — they go (present 3rd pl.) · also ir + gerund 'keep going' (passando van 'they go on passing') · also ir + infinitive 'go to' (le van çercar 'they go to besiege him'; se van tornar 'they go back')
llegando: llegar — arriving, drawing near (gerund; llegando delant 'coming up ahead'; = llegando)
vidie: veer — he saw (imperfect 3rd sg., Pidal's vi[d]ie; de lo que vidie 'of what he saw'; = veía)
era: seer — it was (imperfect of seer = ser) · era + past part. 'had' (ser as pluperfect auxiliary with intransitives; Minaya assí era llegado 'Minaya had arrived')
pagado: pagar — satisfied, pleased; also paid (past part.; será pagado = 'he will be content with')
adelant: adelant — onward, ahead (apocopated adverb; = adelante) · also adelant — henceforth, from now on (of time; mio reyno adelant 'the rest of my reign'); ir adelant 'to prosper, go forward' (las nuevas del Çid mucho van adelant; = prosperar)
catando: catar — looking at, beholding (gerund; archaic for mirar)
vido: veer — he saw (strong preterite 3rd sg.; Pidal's vi[d]o; = vio)
venir: venir — to come (infinitive; = venir) · also venir se a — 'will come about' (split future, venir + se + a = ha; venir se a más por espacio 'will come about later at leisure'; = se vendrá)
díago: Díago — Diego (personal name; Pidal's Dí[a]go; Diego González, one of the two Infantes of Carrión; = Diego)
fernando: Fernando — Fernando, one of the two Infantes of Carrión (also Ferrando; = Fernando)
son: seer — they are (3rd pl.) · also son — perfect auxiliary of intransitives and passive auxiliary (todos son exidos 'have all gone out'; nombrados son; son derramadas 'are scattered')
fijos: fijo — son (masc. pl.; fijos dalgo 'sons of something', noblemen; = hijos) · also fijos — children, sons and daughters together (los yernos e las fijas todos vuestros fijos son)
comde: conde — count (Pidal's co[m]de; al comde de Barçilona 'to the count of Barcelona'; = conde)
don: don — don, lord (honorific title) · also don — gift (noun; en don 'as a gift') · also don — from where, whence (= donde, de onde; Castejón don abremos grand enpara 'Castejón, from which we shall have great protection') · 'whereof, with which' (Pidal 'de lo cual'; don yo sea pagado 'whereof I may be satisfied') · also don — when, where (= donde, of time; Don llegan los otros 'when the others come up')
gonçalvo: Gonçalvo — Gonzalo (Pidal's restored Gonçal[v]o; el conde don Gonçalvo, father of the Infantes of Carrión; = Gonzalo)
fermoso: fermoso — beautiful (f- for h-; = hermoso) · also fermoso — as adverb 'warmly, graciously' (fermoso sonrrisava 'he smiled warmly')
venides: venir — you come (2nd pl. present, old -des ending; = venís)
sodes: seer — you are (2nd pl. present, used respectfully to one person; = sois; old -edes ending, cf. odredes, vedes, catedes)
lidiar: lidiar — to fight (infinitive; = lidiar, closest luchar)
bien: bien — well · bien — good, benefit (noun; algún bien vos pueda far 'some good I may do you') · bien — very, quite, intensifying an adverb (bien çerca del agua 'very near the water')
pagados: pagar — paid, satisfied (past part. masc. pl.; todos sodes pagados 'you are all satisfied'; = pagados)
carrión: Carrión — Carrión de los Condes, town in Palencia, seat of the counts of Carrión (= Carrión)
vos: vos — you (object pronoun, polite/plural) · also subject 'you' (vos, que por mí dexades 'you who leave for my sake'); dative 'to you' (dar vos quiero vuestra part) · also reflexive/ethic 'you (yourselves)' (id vos en algara 'go off on a raid'); dative with an impersonal sense (si cueta vos fore 'if need befall you')
irán: ir — they will go (future 3rd pl.; = irán)
mandados: mandado — message, news, report (pl.; here the tidings that spread; = mandados) · also past part. pl. of mandar 'to grant, bestow', agreeing with the object (çiento ha mandados 'he has given a hundred', of the mounts)
cómmo: commo — how (exclamative; = cómo) · also cómmo — 'how' in an indirect question (veremos cómmo lidia 'we shall see how he fights')
avemos: aver — we have (present 1st pl.; = hemos) · avemos de + inf. 'we must' (mucho avemos de andar 'we have far to go'); avemos qué fablar 'we have something to speak of' · also perfect auxiliary aver + participle (avemos preso 'we have taken')
arrancado: arrancado — routed, driven off (past part. of arrancar, 'to pull out, uproot', here 'to rout'; arrancado es el rey 'the king is routed'; = arrancado, derrotado) · also arrancar — won (of a battle; una lid a arrancado 'he has won a battle'; = ganado)
y: y — and (rarer spelling of e) · also y — there (adverb, = i, Latin ibi; entraré y 'I shall enter there')
santos: santo — saint (masc. pl.); los sos santos 'his saints' · also adjective, holy (los santos padres 'the holy fathers')
desta: de + esta — of this (preposition de + demonstrative fem. sg.; desta batalla 'of this battle'; = de esta)
arrancada: arrancada — rout, headlong flight; also the pursuit and rout of the enemy (de arrancada 'in rout'; el arrancada, el before a vowel-initial fem. noun; = arrancada) · also 'victory' (Pidal's gloss at v. 1233: esta arrancada 'this victory') · also arrancar — won (past part. fem. sg. with aver, agreeing with lid: desta lid que mio Çid ha arrancada 'this battle my Çid has won'; = ganada)
iremos: ir — we shall go (future 1st pl.; iremos adelant 'we shall go onward'; = iremos)
minaya: Minaya — the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called, usually explained as mi + anaya 'my brother'
álbar: Álbar — Álvar (personal name, Álbar Fáñez; = Álvar)
essora: essora — then, at that moment (ess' + ora; en essora 'at that moment'; = entonces)
es: seer — it is (present 3rd sg.) · also ser as perfect auxiliary of intransitives (exido es 'has gone out') and passive auxiliary (la tienda es cogida) · also es — that (apocopated esse = ese, demonstrative; en es alcaz 'in that pursuit', por es logar 'through that place')
trae: traer — he carries, brings (present 3rd sg.) · also trae mal — 'treats badly, harries' (el salido de Castiella así los trae tan mal 'the exile from Castile treats them so badly')
cuello: cuello — neck (= cuello; al cuello 'about his neck' of a mantle worn, and 'by the neck', al cuello lo tomó, Pidal 'lo cogió por el cuello')
lanças: lança — lance; also the horseman who bears it (pl.; = lanzas)
avie: aver — he had (imperfect; unaccented spelling beside avié) · also aver — impersonal temporal 'it had been' (passado avie tres años 'three years had passed'; = hacía/habían pasado)
recabdo: recabdo — care, precaution, strict order (= recaudo) · also recabdo — business secured, a sure outcome (con todo buen recabdo 'with everything well in hand') · recabdo — account, reckoning (oro e plata que non saben recabdo 'gold and silver past all reckoning') · also con recabdo — within bounds, under control (non es con recabdo el dolor de Valençia 'the grief of Valencia is past all bounds') · also todo el recabdo está 'every precaution is taken' (Pidal: 'hay toda clase de precauciones'; en Medina todo el recabdo está)
aquellos: aquel — those (masc. pl. demonstrative; con aquellos que 'with those who'; = aquellos)
gelos: ge + los — them to him (ge, ancestor of modern se, + los; = se los) · also ge = 'to them' (que gelos diessen 'that they should give them to them', the knights) · also ge 'from him', dative of separation (gelos reçibe 'he receives them from him')
dieran: dar — they had given (pluperfect in -ra; = habían dado) · also non ge los dieran en don 'they had not given them to him as a gift' (= no se los habían dado)
gelo: ge + lo — it to him/them (ge, ancestor of modern se, + lo; = se lo)
ayuso: ayuso — down, downward (adverb, Latin deorsum; no modern equivalent, closest abajo)
destellando: destellar — dripping, trickling (gerund; la sangre destellando 'the blood dripping'; Latin destillare; closest destilando, since modern destellar means 'to flash')
moros: moro — Moor (masc. pl.); a moros nin a cristianos, 'to any living soul' (merism)
grado: grado — thanks (grado a … 'thanks be to …') · also grado — will, good will (de grado 'willingly, gladly'; de grado non avrié nada, 'of good will there would be nothing to be had') · en grado tener 'to be thankful for' (en grado vos lo tengo 'I thank you for it')
padre: padre — father · el Padre santo, God the Father
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour' · al ora 'at that very hour, then' (en ti crovo al ora) · also una grant ora — a long while (Pidal 'un gran rato'; = un buen rato)
fostes: seer — you were (archaic 2nd pl. preterite of ser, used respectfully to one person; = fuestes)
nado: nacer — born (past part.; = nacido); omne nado, 'man born', an all-inclusive idiom like moros nin cristianos
canpo: canpo — field, battlefield (en canpo 'in the field, in battle'; = campo)
vuestros: vuestro — your (masc. pl.; = vuestros) · also los vuestros — 'your men' (possessive with article as a noun; vos con los vuestros 'you with your men')
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira') · lo so — 'what is his, his own' (neuter article + possessive; lo so puede menguar 'what is his may dwindle') · also so — their (so consejo 'their counsel', so vino 'their wine'; = su)
preçiados: preçiado — valuable, precious (adj. masc. pl.; from preçiar; = preciados)
ellos: ellos — they, them (stressed 3rd pl. masc. pronoun)
ganados: ganar — gained, earned (past part. masc. pl., agreeing with its object, as with ovo bastidos; avien ganados = habían ganado) · also ganados — gains, spoils (noun, masc. pl.; Pidal 'ganancias': los ganados que fizo 'the gains he made'; = ganancias)
valençia: Valençia — Valencia, the Moorish kingdom and city whose king Tamín is addressed (= Valencia) · also Valençia — the city itself, held by the Cid (en Valençia sedí mio Çid 'in Valencia was my Cid'; Valençia vienen çercar 'they come to besiege Valencia')
raçión: raçión — share, portion (fem. noun; non ayan i raçión, Pidal 'no tomen parte en la batalla'; closest parte; not the modern 'ration')
çientos: çiento — hundred (masc., pl. in compounds; seys çientos 'six hundred'; = cientos, modern seiscientos)
aver: aver — wealth, property, goods (noun use of aver, beside aver the verb 'to have') · also aver — to have (infinitive; aver … de + inf. 'to be bound to', split conditional aver vos lo iedes de far 'you would be bound to do it')
tenien: tener — they held; with armas, they played at arms (imperfect 3rd pl. in -ién; armas tenien 'they played at arms', Pidal 'jugaban las armas'; = tenían) · also tener 'hold, reckon' (commo ellos tenien 'as they reckoned it', imperfect 3rd pl.; = tenían, pensaban)
salvo: salvo — safety, safe-keeping (noun; en vuestro salvo 'in your safe keeping') · also adjective, safe, saved (por end es salvo de mal 'for that reason he is saved from evil')
serien: seer — they would be (conditional 3rd pl., -ien ending; non serien allí llegados 'they would not have come there (of their own will)'; = serían)
foron: seer — they were (preterite 3rd pl., variant of fueron; = fueron) · also foron — they went (ir, which shares this preterite; F[o]ron los mandados a todas partes 'the messages went everywhere')
conduchos: conducho — provisions, victuals (masc. pl.; conduchos largos 'abundant provisions'; = víveres, provisiones)
alegres: alegre — glad, happy (pl.; todos son alegres 'all are glad'; = alegres)
